title: A king from Napata (Cush) conquers Upper Egypt
summary: A king from Napata (Cush) conquers Upper Egypt
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). Dated only by the Generations books cited below; no tier 1–4 chronology covers this event.

sorting_basis.note: PROVISIONAL: no CFAH, Ussher–Jones or Ussher date exists, so the sort uses Generations (Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), PDF p. 416): 778–713 BC. Pending owner decision (open question A8).

chronologies.note: King Kashta ruled from Thebes until 740 BC.
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "778–713 BC" (PDF p. 416): 28 years earlier (ranges overlap).

chronologies.date: “the Ethiopian was lord of the land for fifty years”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.137 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 155 (PDF p. 157)
chronologies.note: Sabacos the Ethiopian displaces the blind Anysis; foretold as fifty years (2.139). Generations (provisional) dates the Kushite conquest of Egypt about 778 BC under a different king; Herodotus gives no year.
